chapter: Earl Hines, Chicago and later gigs
title: The colored hotel above the Grand Terrace
summary: Visiting black bands stayed at the hotel next to the Grand Terrace, and musicians jammed in the rooms.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah, we -- this is the days when Chicago was really jumping because there was a theater -- I mean a hotel right over the Grand Terrace. And the Grand Terrace was right on the corner of South Parkway and Oakwood Boulevard. Now, the Grand Terrace was right under the L, right underneath the L around the corner.

And all the guys used to stay at this hotel. It was a colored hotel. I don't know, I forgot the name of the hotel but it's right on the corner. And Fats Waller used to stay there, and everybody. Every colored performed came in town, they would -- Duke and his band, they would live there. Cab and his band. I never forgot Duke's band. They used to travel a lot by train, and they would bring trunks -- because I see them bring these big trunks when they'd come into Chicago to the hotel.

And that's how we got to hang around with a lot of these guys, and we knew them all because they would hang out there. And we would even go in the rooms and jam. Get a guitar player and go in the rooms in this hotel. You could hear music all over that hotel. And we'd find our own spots and just jam. It was a lot of fun.
